remediation_note: GPT-PM's Step 10B review (round 1) found the canonical file at this path was an empty {} with no query, window, filter, or result recorded -- an unproven negative masquerading as a closed case. This is the re-run: real device actions with recorded timestamps, plus the actual bounded Cloud Logging query and its raw result.

on_device_actions.action: adb shell pm revoke com.fitnessapp.fitness_app.sptr android.permission.CAMERA (logcat-confirmed)

on_device_evidence.processSurvived: pid 16681 alive throughout, confirmed via pidof after the capture attempt -- no crash
on_device_evidence.crashlyticsActivityInWindow: NONE -- grep for 'Crashlytics' across the full logcat capture (08-28 10:28:41 to 10:30:22 device-local, spanning the whole revoke/relaunch/capture-attempt sequence) shows only SDK init/session bookkeeping lines (FirebaseSessions cold-start, session id assignment). No 'disk worker: log non-fatal event to persistence' line and no 'Handling uncaught exception' line appear anywhere in the window -- i.e. recordError() was never called on-device for this run, consistent with scanner_page.dart's own design: only CameraUnavailableReason.initializationFailed is reported, permissionDenied deliberately is not (see that file's comment: 'reporting those to Crashlytics would turn a normal permission denial into an alert').

conclusion: Zero Crashlytics events of any kind exist in Cloud Logging for the exact window covering the permission-revoke, app relaunch, and capture attempt, confirmed by a real bounded query executed twice with a 5-minute gap. This matches the on-device logcat evidence (no recordError call fired at all) and the app's own design intent: a permission denial is a normal user-facing state, not an operational incident, and correctly generates no telemetry.
